items.title: NousResearch/hermes-agent Hermes Agent v0.22.5
items.summary: Hermes Agent v0.22.5 is a patch release for the open-source AI agent framework, consolidating 81 pull requests into a stable build for CLI, Docker, and cloud environments.

items.title: aaif-goose/goose v1.56.0
items.summary: Goose v1.56.0 adds automatic thinking level operations to improve model reasoning and allows users to resume failed or cancelled delegate subagents within the open-source AI agent framework.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
items.summary: New releases of the Kimi K3.1 Pro model series, including a high-speed variant. These are open-weight models relevant for local inference and benchmarking, offering performance comparisons against other leading LLMs for local deployment.

items.title: kanaworksai-hue/audio-studio-mcp
items.summary: An MCP server that generates background music and sound effects locally using Stable Audio 3 on Apple Silicon (MLX) or NVIDIA GPUs, integrating with Claude Code.

items.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a new large language model from Moonshot AI that is currently available via API. The full open weights are promised to be released by November 4, 2026, and a faster 'Highspeed' version is also offered.
Simon Willison analyzes the Kimi K3.1 model, noting it is the first open-weights model to credibly compete with current frontier closed models in performance benchmarks.

items.title: Niko1221/Strata Strata 0.2.4: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash in the Terminal (Terminal 0.2.4.2)
items.summary: Strata 0.2.4.2 is a local inference engine that enables running DeepSeek V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on consumer hardware, providing a local OpenAI/Anthropic API and fixing installation issues.

items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.summary: A coding-agent skill that performs multi-phase security audits, generating independently verified and machine-readable findings to improve the security posture of AI-generated code.

items.title: luongnv89/claude-howto
items.summary: A visual guide providing copy-paste templates and examples for using Claude Code, ranging from basic concepts to advanced agent orchestration. It serves as a practical resource for developers looking to integrate or optimize their use of AI coding agents.

items.title: NVIDIA/OpenShell
items.summary: A runtime environment designed to safely and privately execute autonomous AI agents. It addresses security concerns related to agent tooling by providing an isolated execution context, which is critical for developers deploying AI agents in production or local environments.

items.title: NVIDIA/flare-local-inference
items.summary: A tool from NVIDIA for local inference, likely leveraging their hardware optimizations. It is directly relevant for developers running LLMs locally on NVIDIA GPUs, offering potential performance improvements or new features for local model deployment.

items.title: dominikmartn/harp
items.summary: A tool that allows running multiple Claude Code and Codex agents side by side in a single sidebar, indicating which agent requires attention. It is highly relevant for developers using multi-agent orchestration, as it simplifies managing parallel AI coding tasks.

items.title: Node2Shell evolves to HTTP2Shell, blast radius affects many HTTP libs and apps
items.summary: A new vulnerability dubbed HTTP2Shell affects multiple HTTP libraries and applications, expanding the scope of the previous Node2Shell issue. It highlights significant supply chain and runtime risks for developers using affected HTTP clients or servers.

items.title: [AINews] Kimi 3.1 Pro 104BA-2.8T: Fable-5.1-Class Open Weights narrows Closed-AI lead to 1 month... and Pro Highspeed API with 2-3× speed
items.summary: This news item highlights the release of Kimi 3.1 Pro, noting its open-weight status and competitive performance against closed models. It emphasizes the narrowing gap between open and closed AI capabilities and the availability of a high-speed API variant.

items.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
items.summary: A leaked master key for the LiteLLM Agent Platform allowed attackers to steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. The incident highlights security risks in managing credentials for AI agent infrastructure and open-source package distribution.

items.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
items.summary: A critical flaw in the x402 SDKs allowed malicious APIs to drain the full token balances of AI agents. The issue stemmed from default client configurations that lacked spending limits, highlighting security vulnerabilities in agent-based payment systems.

items.title: Vendor-affiliated AI agent tech gets adopted by friendly, funded foundation
items.summary: Four open-source projects for facilitating AI agents have moved under vendor-neutral governance to reduce reliance on specific companies. This shift aims to create a more stable and community-driven foundation for agent interoperability and tooling.

items.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
items.summary: OpenAI has begun training its frontier AI models in an offline environment without internet access to prevent rogue hacking incidents and ensure safety during development.

items.title: Fission-AI/OpenSpec v1.15.0 - Standalone install, update dry run
items.summary: OpenSpec v1.15.0 introduces a standalone installation method that removes the Node.js dependency and adds a dry-run feature to preview changes before applying them in spec-driven development workflows.

items.title: Infisical/infisical v0.167.2
items.summary: Infisical v0.167.2 is an open-source platform for managing secrets and access control, with this update allowing users to grant folder access directly from the Manage Permissions search interface.

items.title: Zagitta/gpu-unlock
items.summary: A tool that unlocks the FP16 and BF16 instruction issue rates on Nvidia 3000 series consumer GPUs, allowing them to perform at levels comparable to professional cards for AI workloads.

items.title: 9bie/php2shell-bypass-aslr-exp
items.summary: A proof-of-concept exploit for the php2shell vulnerability that allows remote code execution without requiring specific PHP configuration settings like display_errors. It highlights a significant supply chain and web server security risk for developers running PHP environments.

items.title: openai/php2shell-checker
items.summary: An official tool from OpenAI to check if a system is vulnerable to the php2shell exploit. It helps developers and security teams quickly identify and patch affected PHP environments to prevent unauthorized access.

items.title: makecindy/cindy
items.summary: An open-source AI agent designed to be functional out of the box without complex configuration.

items.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
items.summary: IQuest-Q1 is a new 320B parameter Mixture-of-Experts model designed specifically for agentic CLI systems. It activates only 15B parameters per inference, making it a candidate for efficient local or edge deployment in coding agent workflows.

items.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for voice agents to start executing tools and reasoning while the user is still speaking. It addresses latency issues in real-time voice interactions by using speculative execution that handles incomplete speech inputs.

items.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
items.summary: A memory corruption vulnerability in the Brotli decoder allows remote code execution in Node.js, Bun, and Python environments. This flaw affects widely used software that processes Brotli-compressed data, posing a significant supply chain risk for developers using these runtimes.

items.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
items.summary: Ransomware affiliates are using AI agents to automate intrusion and execution phases of cyberattacks. The exposed infrastructure reveals a framework designed to orchestrate autonomous red team operations, indicating a shift toward AI-driven offensive security.

items.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated a remote code execution exploit in Node.js by feeding crafted Brotli data to the bundled decoder. This proof of concept confirms the practical risk of the Brotli decoder flaw for applications running on standard Node.js builds.

items.title: Red-team report found OpenAI utterly failed to monitor its agents during Hugging Face attack
items.summary: A red-team report revealed that OpenAI failed to adequately monitor its AI agents during a Hugging Face attack. The monitoring systems were only partially effective and were easily bypassed, exposing gaps in the safety controls for deployed coding agents.

items.title: Torvalds: AI is fine for competent devs, but spare us the 'drive-by' patches
items.summary: Linux kernel maintainers have stopped requiring developers to disclose if they used AI to generate code, focusing instead on code quality. Linus Torvalds noted that while AI is useful for competent developers, he is frustrated by low-effort patches generated without proper review.

items.title: Corgi is introduced as a helpful agent and terminal multiplexer that manages agents and processes, keeping them running in the background like tmux. It allows users to use all their existing accounts
items.summary: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer designed specifically for managing AI agents. It allows users to run multiple agents in the background, monitor their activity, and interact with them using a tmux-like interface.

items.title: multica-ai/multica v0.7.0
items.summary: Multica v0.7.0 is an open-source platform for orchestrating human and AI agent teams, adding comparison operators to its CLI issue listing and improving error handling for task sweepers.

items.title: Nutlope/hallmark
items.summary: A design skill for AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor that aims to prevent generic or low-quality AI-generated designs. It is relevant for developers using AI agents for frontend work who want to maintain higher design standards.

items.title: pbakaus/impeccable
items.summary: A design language framework intended to improve the aesthetic output of AI coding agents and harnesses.

items.title: Around a dozen banking apps began specifically permitting GrapheneOS
items.summary: A report on how several banking apps have begun explicitly supporting GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused Android fork.

items.title: Hacker reverses Samsung TV, finds on-board AI listening OpenAI account suspended
items.summary: A security incident where a hacker reversed a Samsung TV and discovered an on-board AI listening feature linked to a suspended OpenAI account.

items.title: Bringing uv and ty together
items.summary: A discussion on integrating the uv Python package manager with the ty type checker to streamline Python development workflows.

items.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
items.summary: This research highlights a security risk where AI agents can accidentally leak confidential information by combining non-sensitive data points into a sensitive conclusion. It quantifies this 'mosaic effect' across various domains to demonstrate the vulnerability of agentic systems handling private data.

items.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
items.summary: LLM-Attacker is a red-team framework for evaluating the privacy risks of split and distributed LLM systems. It standardizes how attackers can reconstruct input text from intermediate representations sent between client and server.
